title: k8s-gpu-upgrade-sim-results-terraform-notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft capturing the results from our k8s+GPU upgrade simulations (lab cluster), plus a set of Terraform module notes and a remediation/rollback playbook. The goal is to produce a repeatable, low-risk upgrade recipe for customer private deployments (VPC & on-prem) that balances driver compatibility, CUDA/NCCL versions, and node pool orchestration.

Background/context:
- Motivation: recent customer requests to run v1.15 models with new CUDA 12 runtime on T4/A10/V100 fleets. We must verify combinations and encode safe upgrade paths into Terraform modules and runbooks.
- Lab cluster: 3x control-plane (kubeadm v1.28), 6x worker (3x A10, 3x T4), OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (kernel 5.19).
- Device plugin: nvidia/k8s-device-plugin v0.12.0 (patched locally for CRI fallback).

Executive summary of findings:
- Safe baseline: kube 1.26 + NVIDIA driver 535.xx + CUDA 11.8 + NCCL 2.16 passes all smoke tests for both T4 and A10 with no memory leaks observed in 24h load run.
- Cutting edge path (kube 1.28 + driver 545 + CUDA 12.1 + NCCL 2.19) is workable for A10 but flaky on older T4 kernels (observed kernel OOPS on one node, likely driver/kernel ABI issue).
- The main failure mode during quick upgrades is mismatched nv_peer_mem and RDMA libs on nodes with Mellanox HCAs — we saw degraded NCCL allreduce throughput.
- Terraform module change required: explicit taint/cordon workflow and a drain-with-grace-period=300s template; previously we used default drain behavior which caused pre-stop timeouts on pods with large KV cache.

Compatibility matrix (representative rows from lab runs):

K8s Version | NVIDIA Driver | CUDA | NCCL | Node HW | Test Result | Notes
------------|---------------|------|------|---------|-------------|------
1.26        | 535.54        | 11.8 | 2.16 | T4      | PASS        | Stable under 24h soak, device-plugin OK
1.26        | 535.54        | 11.8 | 2.16 | A10     | PASS        | Peak perf within expected deltas
1.26        | 545.30        | 12.1 | 2.19 | A10     | PASS-RECOMMEND | Higher throughput but needs kernel 5.19+
1.28        | 545.30        | 12.1 | 2.19 | T4      | FAIL        | Kernel OOPS during heavy allreduce, suspect driver-kernel ABI
1.28        | 540.20        | 12.0 | 2.18 | A10     | PASS-PROBE  | Acceptable, but NCCL microbench shows slight perf regression
1.25        | 520.61        | 11.3 | 2.14 | V100    | PASS-LEGACY  | V100 stack stable, matches previous baselines

Notes on matrix:
- PASS means all validation tests (smoke, perf, stability) succeeded for 24h. PASS-RECOMMEND means we think it's good to push but with kernel/reboot caveats. FAIL indicates either crash/OOM/kernel OOPS. PASS-PROBE means we want an extra 72h soak before recommending.

Validation test list (what we run):
- pod-level: nvidia-smi, dcgm-exporter health, device-plugin registration check
- workload-level: small-batch generation loop (tokens/sec), KV cache warmup + long-chat replay, embedding throughput (64B batches)
- system-level: NCCL allreduce (gather across 3 nodes), RDMA bandwidth check (ib_write_bw), GPU mem pressure test (parallel allocations up to 90%)
- soak tests: 24h traffic replay with intermittent 20% traffic spikes and periodic full-node drains

Terraform module notes (changes to apply):
1) Module: redwood-k8s-gpu-nodepool (v0.9 -> v0.10)
   - New variables: driver_version (string), cuda_version (string), pre_drain_hooks (list<string>), grace_period_seconds (number, default 300)
   - Behavior: when upgrading node pool, module now creates a new pool with desired driver image and cordons old pool first. This supports immutable node replacement for on-prem baremetal via reboot orchestration.
   - Outputs: upgrade_plan_id (string), last_successful_image (string)

2) Module: redwood-device-plugin-helm
   - Pin chart to upstream 0.12.0 but override image to our patched image registry.redwood/inference/nvidia-device-plugin:0.12.0-rw
   - Add post-install Job that verifies plugin registers GPUs on all schedulable nodes. Job fails fast and triggers terraform error handling.

3) Upgrade steps (recommended automation):
   - step 0: schedule maintenance window + notify customers (2 weeks notice for major stack changes)
   - step 1: create a new nodepool with desired driver image and kubelet config (enable cgroup v2 knob if required)
   - step 2: wait for readiness + run device-plugin post-install checks
   - step 3: run smoke validation on new pool (minimal traffic) for 2h; run NCCL allreduce across new nodes
   - step 4: shift 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over configurable ramp window (default 4h) using routing policies in control plane
   - step 5: decommission old pool, drain with grace=300s and run final soak for 24h

Rollback and safety mechanisms:
- Auto-rollback trigger: if 10% of requests see increased latency >2x baseline for 30m or if any kernel OOPS reported on nodes in the new pool, start immediate rollback to previous nodepool image and route traffic back.
- Quick rollback path: Terraform apply with previous driver_version + cuda_version using saved upgrade_plan_id. We keep last_successful_image as a canonical fallback.
- Emergency stop: cordon all nodes in new pool and turn off routing to that pool; if critical, reopen customer traffic to Dedicated fallback (hosted) with automated API keys swap.

Lab run timeline and key artifacts:
- 2025-11-20: baseline runs (kube 1.26 + 535 + 11.8) — artifacts: perf traces, dcgm logs (S3: s3://redwood-lab/gpu/2025-11-20/)
- 2025-12-05: probe runs for 1.28 + 545 stack — observed kernel OOPS on t4-03 node at 2025-12-05T19:12Z (journalctl attached) — ticket INFRA-1973
- 2026-01-18: terraform module prototype merged to infra repo (PR #482) with new nodepool workflow

Concrete checks operators should run pre- and post-upgrade:
Pre-upgrade checklist (short):
- Verify kernel versions across nodes (uname -a) -- must be >= required for chosen driver
- Confirm HCA firmware and OFED versions for RDMA-enabled clusters
- Snapshot cluster state and etcd backup
- Ensure monitoring alerts and tracing are active and baselined

Post-upgrade checklist (short):
- Check device plugin registration on all nodes (kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l app=nvidia-device-plugin)
- Run perf spot checks: tokens/sec, embed throughput -- compare to baseline
- Run NCCL allreduce across representative GPUs and check bandwidth against historic median
- Inspect kernel logs for OOPS/dmesg segfault patterns

Suggested smoke command snippets (lab):
- kubectl -n kube-system logs job/nvidia-device-plugin-postinstall --follow
- kubectl run -i --tty nccl-test --restart=Never --image=registry.redwood/nccl:2.19 --command -- bash -c "mpirun -np 6 ./build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 8192 -f 2"
- ssh node && sudo apt-get install -y ibutils && ib_write_bw mlx5_0

Open questions / risks:
- Can older T4 kernels realistically be upgraded in-place to support driver 545 without full reboots that require lengthy maintenance windows? (ACTION: SRE to validate for vendor X images)
- How aggressive can we be with CUDA 12 adoption for customers with mixed GPU fleets? Recommend per-customer posture: strict (only validated combos), permissive (allow experimental for dev).
- Do we expose driver_version/cuda_version knobs to customers or keep as platform-only managed?

Action items (short):
- Jordan: extend soak run to 72h for the 545+12.1 stack on A10 (due 2026-02-17)
- Sofia: add RDMA/fc firmware checks to pre-upgrade terraform module (due 2026-02-05)
- Ravi: create playbook snippet for emergency kernel OOPS rollback (due 2026-02-03)

Appendix: quick debug logs excerpt (truncated)
- Dec 05 19:12:04 t4-03 kernel: [12345.678901] NVRM: GPU at 00000000:00:1C.0: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x4d)
- Dec 05 19:12:05 t4-03 kernel: [12345.679200] kernel: Unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at virtual address 0000000000000008

Notes to self (todo rough):
- Draft a customer-facing upgrade checklist (one-pager) that includes expected downtime, recommended snapshot cadence, and a compatibility badge for common stack combos.
- Add a regen job that builds and publishes device-plugin patched image on each release of the module.

This doc is intentionally informal. Use linked artifacts for log bundles and PR diffs. Update the matrix below as new lab runs complete.
